Ivy: starting a vermillion48k (int4hybrid) bring-up. target ctx=49152, prefill ~44k. seeing a subtle 'glint' where 2-token snippets from ~43k reappear ~30 tokens later. dump logs.
Kem: repro command:
```
./onboard --model vermillion48k --quant int4hybrid --context 49152 --prefill 44000 --kvcache-mode tiled --rope per-tile
```
Noah: symptom: not full repeats, just tight 2-token echoes that nudge top-k. reproducible ~8% runs.
Sofia: sanitized log:
```
[prefill] pos=43012
[kv] read shard=6 tile=11 idx=2147483650 offset=18446744073709551590
[rope] applied_phase=1.00003 expected=0.99997
[decode] emitted: ... 411 522 411 ...
```
Ivy: offset looks like -106 if treated signed. suspects int32->uint64 leak in tile math.
Kem: bisect says regression introduced in kernel v1.20 where we added "fast-merge" for small tiles to reduce RPCs; that code path skipped a bounds cast in some edge cases.
Noah: perf notes: tiled kvcache + per-tile rope saves ~12% p99. disabling merge reduces glint but hurts latency.
Sofia: hypothesis: merge returns stale tile index during concurrent eviction; per-tile rope phase mismatch yields coherent micro-echo rather than noise.
Ivy: quick mitigation: enable prefill-snapshot=8192 or set --kvcache-merge=0. both avoid glint.
Kem: workaround test: added an atomic fence around merge publish; incidents drop to ~1% but perf hit ~+4%.
Noah: CI: adding svt/vermillion-glint check (assert no 2-token repeats in prefill range 42k..44k).
ci-bot: svt/vermillion-glint (pr/merge-guard)  RUNNING 
Sofia: action items:
- Kem: PR with safe-merge publish + defensive casting and counter for "merge-alias". include microbench.
- Noah: run snapshot breakpoint sweep (4k/8k/16k) and report perf vs repeat-rate.
- Ivy: add 3 gold long prompts to onboarding goldset that capture glint and add nightly run.
- Sofia: prepare customer note for Dedicated canary: recommend --kvcache-merge=0 temporarily during rollout.
Kem: will open PR and include unit test that injects negative-offset into merge reader to ensure fail-fast.
Ivy: thanks all  keep updates short here. :lock:
